Start with the feature you will actually use: the 6-quart Cook & Carry adds programmable timing; the SCV800-B manual model gives you a larger pot. Extra capacity and automatic timing solve different problems.

Programmable 6-quart or manual 8-quart?

DecisionCrock-Pot SCCPVL610-S familyCrock-Pot SCV800-B
Nominal size6 quarts8 quarts
ControlsProgrammable countdownManual High / Low / Warm dial
At the end of cookingAutomatically switches to WarmYou select Warm manually
LidCook & Carry locking-lid designStandard glass lid
Primary reason to choose itTiming convenience and carrying cooked foodLarger batches with simple controls
Main compromiseLess capacity; more control features to checkNo programmed finish or automatic Warm change

Sources: Crock-Pot programmable 6-quart specifications and Crock-Pot SCV800-B product details. The current 6-quart manufacturer page identifies revision SCCPVL610-S-ABR; check the full suffix and manual on the unit you buy.

SCCPVL610-S: choose for the timer, not just the locking lid

The useful upgrade is the automatic move to Warm when the countdown finishes. It can help when your recipe finishes before you plan to serve dinner. The locking lid is for carrying cooked food: follow the supplied manual about opening or releasing the locks during cooking.

Customer feedback: Home Depot reviews dated April 8 and March 29, 2026 report concerns about heat control; the latter also mentions the crock surface. These are individual complaints, not temperature measurements from our own testing. The review page includes feedback for other Crock-Pot models, so we have not treated its combined rating as a score for this exact cooker. Read the 6-quart product reviews and manufacturer responses.

Why choose it: you specifically need programmable timing and a carrying lid. Drawback: a timer does not measure whether food is cooked, and owner concerns make the return terms and replacement-crock availability worth checking.

SCV800-B: choose for larger batches and straightforward controls

The manual 8-quart cooker suits someone who wants more room and is happy to manage the finish time. Do not confuse the Warm position on its dial with a programmable model that moves to that setting automatically.

Customer feedback: on Crock-Pot's SCV800-B page, a February 4, 2024 customer describes enough capacity for family meals and leftovers, with easy cleaning of the removable pot. A March 22, 2022 reviewer values the simple controls and larger size. Those older reports explain its appeal but do not establish current-unit durability. Read SCV800-B customer feedback.

Why choose it: larger recipes and basic controls without paying for timing features you will not use. Drawback: a bigger pot takes more washing and storage space, and you must manage the change from cooking to Warm yourself.

Our recommendation depends on your routine

Choose the programmable 6-quart model when timing convenience solves a real problem and your usual recipes fit that size. Choose the manual 8-quart when you regularly cook larger recipes and can be there to manage the controls. For small portions, compare a smaller cooker rather than assuming an oversized pot is the better deal.

Capacity is not a promise about portions

Six or eight quarts describes nominal vessel capacity, not the amount you should fill to the rim. Use the fill guidance in the exact manual and a recipe appropriate to that cooker. A claim such as “serves ten” cannot account for appetites, side dishes or the shape of a joint.

What to check beyond the purchase price

  • The replacement pot: check that a compatible insert and lid can be sourced using the full model number. A similar-looking crock is not automatically the correct replacement.
  • The sink and cupboard: allow for the handles and the space needed to lift a full insert safely.
  • The cooking method: neither cooker should be assumed to have a stovetop-safe insert. Follow the supplied instructions before searing or exposing stoneware to a different heat source.
  • The running cost: estimate cost from the exact model's rated power and your electricity tariff, but remember the thermostat cycles. A wattage label alone is not a measured cost for a particular recipe.

Does Warm cook the food for you?

Warm is a holding setting, not a substitute for the cooking stage. Follow the manufacturer's food and temperature guidance, and do not copy an unsafe cooking shortcut simply because it appears in a customer review. If an insert cracks or a control appears faulty, stop using the damaged appliance and contact the maker.

How to compare offers fairly

Match the full model suffix, controls and included lid. An 8-quart manual cooker and a 6-quart programmable Cook & Carry are different products, even if both are described simply as a Crock-Pot. Compare delivered price, warranty and condition only after deciding which set of features you need.

How we researched this comparison

We checked these named models and linked owner reports on November 19, 2026. The comparison is research-based, with no claim of our own cooking or temperature tests. Retailer reviews can mix related models; only relevant comments are attributed here, and we have not converted small review samples into reliability rankings. Live offers, revisions and included accessories may differ.
